item.title: Built Different: Why Tigers and Leopards Think Twice About Dholes
item.description:
Deep in Asia's forests, a pack of dogs the size of a Labrador makes tigers and leopards change their behavior. This documentary breaks down why — not through dramatic claims, but through what pack coordination, numbers, and hunting strategy actually do to a solo apex predator's odds.
What you'll learn: - How dholes use pack coordination to out-strategize prey many times their size - Why their whistle-based communication is functionally unique among canids - What field research says about dhole-tiger encounters — and what's exaggeration - Why dholes are vanishing faster than the predators that avoid them
